label: 60W 802.3bt Type 3 multi-gig PoE injector
description: Single-port 802.3bt Type 3 injector that negotiates up to 60 W at 56 V across all four pairs and carries 2.5G data, sized for Wi-Fi 6/6E APs and heaters/PTZ domes. Because it is a true bt PSE with LLDP and class-based power, it will only hand out 60 W to a device that asks for it.

poe.note: Data sheet output table, POE60U-1BT-2-R column: "Output Power 60W @40°C; 30W @50°C" (read 2026-11-21); the product page heads it "IEEE802.3bt PoE Injector - Single-Port - 60W" with "Power/Port - 60" (https://www.phihong.com/products/power-over-ethernet/poe60u-1bt-2-r/). One port, so the device total is the port ceiling. 60 W is the 40 °C rating: the same sheet derates the unit to 30 W at 50 °C, which the engine models as one published ceiling rather than an ambient-dependent curve.

notes: STANDARD CLAIM, corrected 2026-11-20. The vendor page heads the product "IEEE802.3bt PoE Injector - Single-Port - 60W - 2.5G", lists "Compliant with IEEE802.3bt Standard" and "Power/Port - 60" (https://www.phihong.com/products/power-over-ethernet/poe60u-1bt-2-r/, read 2026-11-20), and the POE60U-1BT data sheet's Detection Standards row reads "Output #1 - IEEE802.3af/at/bt, Output #2 - IEEE802.3af/at/bt" with "Total Output Power 60W @ 40C" (https://www.phihong.com/wp-content/uploads/POE60U-1BT-X-R.pdf, read 2026-11-20) - so all three are named, as the sheet names them. It declared `802.3at` alone beside a 60 W port, and 802.3at's PSE ceiling is 30 W (Cisco Catalyst 9000 PoE Configuration Guide, Table 1: https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/switches/lan/c9000/infra/poe/poe-configuration-guide/g-poe/c-poe.html). The file contradicted itself before this: its `role` already read "802.3bt-type-3". test/poe-injector-standard.test.js holds the rule.
